pastebox: let pastes expire

pastebox keeps every paste until someone deletes it, and the issue reports a disk 90% full. This guided plan lets the writer pick when a paste expires, deletes expired pastes in a cleanup job, and keeps never as the default.

  1. DecidedA paste can expire after 1 hour, 1 day or 1 week. Never stays the default.03
  2. ChangeThe new paste form gets an Expires after choice.03
  3. ChangeThe table gets an expires_at column, and an expired paste answers 410.04
  4. ChangeA cleanup job deletes expired pastes every 10 minutes.04
  5. KeptPastes saved before the change never expire, and deleting by hand works as before.05
  6. OpenShould an expired paste answer 404 from the start?06

01 / 06Why pastes need to expire

Every paste, kept forever

pastebox keeps a paste until someone deletes it, and almost nobody does. The issue reports a disk 90% full and asks for pastes that expire.

Where pastes are kept

Every paste is one row in the pastes table: an id, the text, and when it was saved. Nothing records how long to keep it.

What the issue asks

A choice on the form, with never as the default, so nothing changes for anyone who does not pick.

02 / 06Where expiry reaches

Three places change

The form gets a choice, the table gets a column, and the server reads it before it answers. A new cleanup job removes what has expired.

The path of one paste

The writer picks a time on the form. The server stores it beside the text, and checks it again on every read.

03 / 06The form

One new choice, never by default

The new paste form gets an Expires after choice: 1 hour, 1 day, 1 week, or never. Never is selected first, so someone who does not look keeps today's behaviour.

04 / 06The server and the table

Expired pastes answer 410

The pastes table gets an expires_at column. Reading a paste whose time has passed answers 410 Gone, and a cleanup job runs every 10 minutes to delete it.

The check on every read

Today a read answers 404 when the row is missing. The expiry check goes right beside it. The raw route calls the same function, so it gets the check too.

A paste's life

Once its time passes, a paste answers 410. The cleanup job then deletes the row, and the same link answers 404.

05 / 06What stays the same

Old pastes never expire

The new column stays empty for every paste saved before this change, so those pastes are kept as they are today. Deleting a paste by hand works as before.

06 / 06Open question

One answer that changes mid-way

Should an expired paste answer 404 from the start?

As written, an expired paste answers 410 until the cleanup job runs, then 404. Answering 404 from the start means the answer never changes. The maintainers decide before the release.
